correctness.rationale: PASS: Exact factorial moments E(S_n)_j=(n)_j(lambda/n)^j for 0<=j<=k follow from k-wise independence. Uniform integrability below k: E[(S_n)_j 1_{S_n>R}] <= E(S_n)_{j+1}/(R-j), and bounded continuous truncation plus monotone convergence gives kth moment inequality. For sufficiency, truncate target and Poisson at n (move tail to zero), form (1-eps_n)mu^[n]+eps_n pi^[n], eps_n=sqrt(t_n+1/n); lower factorial errors O(1/n) and fixed masses at 0..k at least c_i eps_n. If top moment deficit delta>0, add q_n=d_n/(n)_k at n and correct moments 0..k-1 at 0..k-1 using invertible falling-factorial triangular matrix with diagonal j!; low-order added errors O(n^-1) and q_n=O(n^-k). If delta=0, correct all moments 0..k at 0..k; needed O(t_n+n^-1)=o(eps_n), preserving positivity. Uniform random subset of exact count transforms factorial moments into all-one joint events and inclusion-exclusion proves full k-wise independence. The tail ratio (Y)_j/(Y)_k <= (n-k+1)^-(k-j) for Y>n secures o(n^-1) when j<k. Algebra and moment-correction bounds independently reviewed; no finite sampling inference.
